text:
Alex: Heads up — saw a reproducible latency spike on multi-GPU TP runs when we enable fused attention + QKV sharding. Occurs with variable-length batches and KV-cache warmup.

Priya: Can you paste the profiler snippet? Is it NCCL stalls or compute imbalance? :thinking:

Alex: Profiler shows long waits in a QKV all-gather step right before flash-attn op. Stack looks like:
```
TP-rank0: all_gather_qkv start
  enqueue: ncclAllGather(...)
  wait: cudaEventElapsed 12.8ms
flash_attn_forward start
```
Note the all_gather is blocking the next-token generation.

Matt: Are we doing per-token all-gather on new KV, or per-layer? If per-token, that's gonna blow up with TP>1.

Alex: It's per-layer but we currently do an all-gather of full QKV shards every time we flush prefix into the KV cache. When sequences are uneven we hit cross-shard boundary more often — causes small, frequent NCCL messages (many small all-gathers).

Sara: That rings a bell — earlier microbench showed NCCL latency is dominated by startup for small payloads. We should batch small all-gathers or use async overlap with compute.

infra-bot: deploy-note: profiling build 1763527001 ran on 8xA100-c5.

Priya: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) change kernel selection to fallback (non-fused QKV path) for very small payloads so we can fuse communication and compute differently, 2) adapt batching heuristic to group by seq_len within a request window so fewer shard-crossing events.

Matt: Fallback to non-fused might help because it lets us reorder ops: we can start an async nccl all-gather for KV while compute does head-projection for local shards. Fused flash-attn bundles everything so we lose overlap.

Alex: Agreed. Also KV-cache behavior: currently each token append triggers a full-shard sync for its layer's KV. We should only all-gather the slices required for the next compute step, and keep per-shard local cache for hits. That reduces chattiness.

bench-bot: Microbench numbers (p95 latency):
Before: median 42ms, p95 128ms, TP=2, batch mix (8/32/128)
After (group-by-seq_len + async allgather): median 33ms, p95 96ms (roughly 1.25–1.33x perf)
Details: small message penalty ~9–12ms per NCCL op.

Sara: For longer-term: consider QKV layout change so KV stays colocated with the TP shard that serves most queries (affinity). That reduces cross-shard traffic for common prefixes. But it's a heavier change to rollout with model sharding invariant.

Priya: Implementation plan:
- Short-term (canary): add heuristic to detect small all-gather payloads (< X KB) and switch to async-nccl + compute overlap path.
- Mid-term: implement group-by-sequence-length batching in the request router (coalesce within 10ms window).
- Long-term: explore KV-affinity layout + smarter per-token delta all-gather.

Alex: I'll open a PR for the async overlap first. Need volunteers to review kernel-selection fallback (Priya?) and router change (Matt/Sara).

Matt: Happy to take router changes. I'll mock request grouping and run perf suite.

Priya: I'll sketch kernel fallback patch tonight. If we can reuse the existing kernel registry we can flip a flag per-batch.

Alex: One more datapoint — the spike is worse on V100-like networks (higher per-op latency). So change is high-impact for Dedicated/Private customers on older infra.

Sara: Okay. Action items: Alex -> PR for async all-gather overlap; Priya -> kernel fallback sketch; Matt -> grouping prototype + perf runs; bench-bot -> run regression harness across TP=2,4 on A100/V100. I'll file a small canary rollout for us to test.

Alex: Thanks all. Leaving the profiler snippet + nccl trace in the thread. If anyone finds a quick config toggle to reduce chattiness, drop it here. :thumbsup:
